CSAK LÁTSZÓLAG EGY KIBASZOTT KUP LERÁJ, AMIBEN BOMBA ROBBANT. TULAJDONKÉPPEN EGY ZSENIÁLIS RENDSZER. A RÁHANGOLÓDÁSBAN SEGÍT A FÉNYKÉPE.

source.text: ÁÁÁ!!! BASSZAMEG EGY KAUKÁZUSI FÉRFI SZÁRÍTOTT MÚMIÁJA, BAZMEG!!!
FÚJ!... A BELSŐ SZERVEI ITT ÁZNAK EGY AKVÁRIUMBAN! A SZÍV KÜLÖN EGY LEKVÁROS ÜVEGBEN! FÚJ BAZMEG!

scene.summary: A bearded grandson asks his grandmother where his late grandfather Tibor's oilcloth satchel might be. The grandmother directs him to the shed, admitting it is an utter mess but claiming it has an ingenious underlying system, handing him a photo of Tibor to help him get into the right mindset. As the grandson enters the shed, he discovers increasingly bizarre and horrific items—a helicopter turbine concealing a staircase, a dried human mummy from an old land boundary dispute, and internal organs preserved in an aquarium and a jam jar. The grandmother fondly reminisces in her armchair about how meticulous Tibor was.

characters.name: grandmother
characters.description: An elderly woman sitting comfortably in an armchair, wearing round glasses with wild fluffy hair. She speaks calmly and fondly of her late husband Tibor, using casual swearing and nonchalantly explaining dark secrets without any distress.

characters.name: bearded man
characters.description: A younger man with an undercut, topknot, and a thick black beard, presumably the grandson. He starts out looking for butterfly-collecting gear and ends up screaming in terror off-panel from inside the shed.

panels.description: The bearded man stands by the doorway talking to his grandmother, who is seated in a large armchair. She tells him the satchel should be in the shed, eliciting a worried reaction from him.
The grandmother holds up a framed photograph of the late Tibor papa, explaining that the shed may look like a chaotic bomb site, but is actually an ingenious system.
The bearded man has gone off-panel into the shed and asks if he is seeing a helicopter turbine; the grandmother pleasantly confirms that the stairs begin right behind it.

From inside the shed, the bearded man screams in terror at finding the dried mummy of a Caucasian man. The grandmother thinks or murmurs serenely to herself about a past property dispute ('telekvita').

The bearded man yells in disgust from the shed that preserved organs are soaking in an aquarium and the heart is in a jam jar. The grandmother points a finger up fondly, noting how meticulous Tibor was.

notes: 'Sufni' (shed/lean-to) is a classic trope in Hungarian culture: a chaotic backyard shed packed with decades of hoarded junk, tools, and spare parts that only the patriarch of the house understands.
'Kupleráj' literally means a brothel, but is universally used in Hungarian as slang for an extreme mess or pigsty; 'kibaszott kupleráj' means a 'fucking shambles'.

'Telekvita' (boundary dispute / real estate dispute) is a deadpan, dark punchline in panel p3: grandmother casually recalls that the dried corpse in the shed is simply the victim of a property line conflict between neighbours that Tibor resolved by murdering and mummifying him.

Contrast between the grandson's escalating horror ('BASSZAMEG', 'FÚJ BAZMEG') and the grandmother's sweet, affectionate nostalgia ('Tiborom precíz ember volt!') about her late husband keeping preserved organs neatly separated in jam jars.
